speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with a limp and localized pain. Can you point to the exact spot on your body where it hurts, and what do you think might have caused this?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful, thank you. Since the pain is in the knee but the child is favoring his leg, do you feel the pain specifically when you bend the knee, or does it hurt more in the thigh or hip area? Also, have you noticed any swelling or redness on that side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE). The presentation of a limp with knee pain that is actually referred from the hip, in a child with no fever or trauma, is classic for SCFE. I am requesting an X-ray of the left hip. REQUEST IMAGES: Left Hip X-Ray (AP and Frog-Lateral views).
